post.caption: In 1934 a 726 carat diamond was found on Jacobus Jonker's farm in South Africa and named the Jonker. Harry Winston bought the uncut stone in 1935 and chose New York cutter Lazare Kaplan, who studied it for about a year. Lloyd's of London would not insure the cutting. The largest gem was a 142.90 carat emerald cut, later recut to 125.35 carats, and Winston toured the cut stone across the United States.
